examples.solution_text:
(a) Read the left end of $C$'s bar: its earliest start is $3$ days.

(b) The solid bar runs from $3$ to $7$:
$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Duration}(C)&=7-3\\&=4\text{ days}\end{aligned}$

The dashed marker runs from $7$ to $10$:
$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Float}(C)&=10-7\\&=3\text{ days}\end{aligned}$

(c) Activities $B$, $D$ and $E$ have no dashed markers, so they have zero float. Their bars run end to end from $0$ to $5$, $5$ to $10$ and $10$ to $14$. The critical path is $B$–$D$–$E$.

(d) Read the end of the final bar: the minimum completion time is $14$ days. Activities overlap, so do not add all the bar lengths.

examples.derivation: Earliest activity intervals are A: 0–4, B: 0–6, C: 4–12, D: 6–10, E: 6–11, F: 12–15 and G: 11–14. Completion is 15 days. Backward scanning gives latest event times Start=0, P=4, Q=7, R=12, T=12 and Finish=15. Total floats are A=0, B=1, C=0, D=2, E=1, F=0 and G=1 day. The critical path is A–C–F. Every bar and dashed marker agrees with these results.

C starts at 3 days, has duration 7−3=4 days and float 10−7=3 days. With every non-critical marker explicitly supplied, B, D and E have zero float. Their intervals 0–5, 5–10 and 10–14 span the project, giving critical path B–D–E and minimum completion time 14 days.

A finishes at 6 and B at 2, so C and D both start at 6. C finishes at 11 and D at 9; E therefore starts at 11 and finishes at 15. E's latest start is 11, so D's latest start is 11−3=8 and its total float is 8−6=2 days. The solution correctly retains D's bar from 6 to 9 and adds its dashed marker from 9 to 11.
